t: Which of the following is an example of a non-employer-employee group?
o: Permanent staff of a cement manufacturing company
Officers of a public sector bank
Employees of a state government department
Home-loan borrowers of a housing finance company
e: Borrowers of a lender form a non-employer-employee (affinity) group; the other three are all employer-employee groups where the employer is the master policyholder.

t: Under an employer-employee group term policy, on the death of a covered employee the claim amount is ultimately paid to:
o: The employer for its own use as key-person compensation
The nominee or beneficiary of the deceased employee, routed through the master policyholder
The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation
The insurer's claims reserve as the policy is a pure risk contract
e: The employer holds the master policy as a trustee or agent for the members; the benefit belongs to the employee's nominee or legal heirs, not to the employer.

t: Under IRDAI's group insurance guidelines, the insurer must provide each insured member of a group with:
o: A copy of the complete master policy document
A duplicate of the proposal form signed by the master policyholder
A certified copy of the trust deed
A certificate of insurance setting out the benefits and key terms
e: The master policy is issued to the group policyholder, but each member must receive a certificate of insurance evidencing the cover, the benefit and the important conditions.

t: Which of the following statements is correct about premium collected by a master policyholder from members of a group?
o: It must be passed on to the insurer in full; the master policyholder cannot retain any part of it
The master policyholder may retain up to 5% as service charge
It may be invested by the master policyholder until the policy anniversary
It belongs to the master policyholder until the certificate of insurance is issued
e: IRDAI guidelines prohibit the group policyholder from retaining or diverting any portion of the premium collected from members; the entire premium must be remitted to the insurer.

t: Profit sharing (experience refund) on a group term insurance policy is permitted by IRDAI only in the case of:
o: Non-employer-employee groups above 500 lives
Groups formed by microfinance institutions
Groups where the premium is paid entirely by the members
Employer-employee groups
e: Profit sharing based on favourable claims experience is allowed for employer-employee groups. In non-employer-employee groups it is prohibited, since the organiser could otherwise benefit at the members' expense.

t: In a non-employer-employee group insurance arrangement, which statement is correct regarding payments to the group organiser?
o: The organiser may charge members an administration fee of its choice
The organiser can receive only the commission or remuneration permitted by regulations, and this must be disclosed
The organiser may retain any experience refund declared by the insurer
The organiser is entitled to a share of the insurer's investment income on the premium
e: IRDAI norms restrict payments to the group organiser to regulated commission or remuneration, which must be transparent. The organiser cannot load members with additional charges or retain refunds.

t: A gratuity scheme funded through a life insurer, where the employer's contributions are credited to a policy account that earns a declared interest rate, is classified under IRDAI product regulations as a:
o: Group term product
Group savings-linked product
Fund-based (variable) group non-linked product
Group health product
e: Gratuity, superannuation and leave-encashment funding policies with a policy account earning declared interest are fund-based group non-linked (variable) products, distinct from pure group term cover.

t: The abbreviation OYRGTA used in Indian group life business stands for:
o: One Year Reducing Group Term Assurance
One Year Renewable Group Term Assurance
Optional Yearly Renewable Group Term Annuity
Ordinary Yearly Rated Group Term Assurance
e: OYRGTA is a one-year renewable group term assurance: pure death cover for 12 months, renewed annually with premium re-rated on the current membership and claims experience.

t: In a group term scheme, the 'free cover limit' refers to:
o: The sum assured up to which a member is covered without medical underwriting
The sum assured provided free of premium to the master policyholder
The maximum claim the insurer will pay in one policy year
The cover granted to members who have left the employer
e: Members whose sum assured falls within the free cover limit are accepted without medical evidence; amounts above it require individual underwriting. The limit depends on group size and average sum assured.

t: The 'actively at work' condition in a group term policy means that a member is covered from the date of entry only if:
o: The member has completed one year of service
The member has paid his share of premium
The member has submitted a medical report
The member is at work performing normal duties on that date and not absent due to illness or injury
e: The actively-at-work requirement screens out members who are already sick or disabled when cover starts, serving as a simple underwriting safeguard for the free cover limit.

topic: Investment Pattern for Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: The rate of interest declared by EPFO on provident fund accumulations for the financial year 2024-25 was:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The Central Board of Trustees retained 8.25% for 2024-25, the same as for 2023-24; 8.15% applied for 2022-23 and 8.10% for 2021-22.

t: In a group credit life insurance scheme covering borrowers of a bank, the sum assured for a member typically:
o: Remains level for the full loan tenure
Increases each year in line with interest accrued
Reduces in line with the outstanding loan balance
Is equal to the original loan amount plus processing fees
e: Credit life is designed so that on death the outstanding loan is repaid; hence the cover usually reduces in step with the loan repayment schedule, which also keeps the premium low.

t: An employer wishes to replace its EDLI contribution with a group term insurance policy from a life insurer. Which condition applies?
o: No approval is needed as EDLI is voluntary
The employer must obtain exemption under Section 17(2A) of the EPF Act and the insurer's benefits must be more favourable than EDLI
The employer must obtain IRDAI's approval for the substitution
The policy must be taken only from LIC of India
e: Section 17(2A) of the EPF & MP Act permits exemption from EDLI if the employer provides a scheme with benefits not less favourable; this is granted by the PF authorities, not IRDAI, and any life insurer may offer it.

t: A company covers 500 employees under a group term policy with a uniform sum assured of ₹10 lakh each. The insurer quotes a rate of ₹1.20 per ₹1,000 sum assured. The annual premium is:

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: For an employee covered by the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the gratuity exempt under Section 10(10) of the Income-tax Act is the least of:
o: Actual gratuity, ₹10 lakh and one month's salary per year of service
Actual gratuity, ₹25 lakh and half month's salary per year of service
Actual gratuity, ₹20 lakh and 15/26 of last drawn salary for each completed year or part exceeding six months
Actual gratuity, ₹20 lakh and 10 months' average salary
e: Section 10(10)(ii) exempts the least of the actual amount, the statutory ceiling of ₹20 lakh and the amount computed under the Act's formula of 15 days' wages (15/26 of monthly wages) per year of service.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: A private-sector employee covered by the Payment of Gratuity Act receives gratuity of ₹25 lakh on retirement. The amount computed under the Act's formula is ₹22 lakh. The taxable gratuity is:
o: Nil
₹5 lakh
₹3 lakh
₹25 lakh
e: Exemption is the least of ₹25 lakh (actual), ₹22 lakh (formula) and ₹20 lakh (ceiling) = ₹20 lakh. Taxable = ₹25 lakh − ₹20 lakh = ₹5 lakh.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: An employer's contribution to an approved gratuity fund is allowed as a business deduction under which section of the Income-tax Act, 1961?
o: Section 36(1)(iv)
Section 80C
Section 40A(7)
Section 36(1)(v)
e: Section 36(1)(v) allows contributions to an approved gratuity fund created under an irrevocable trust. Section 36(1)(iv) relates to recognised PF and approved superannuation funds, and Section 40A(7) disallows mere provisions for gratuity.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: With effect from 1 April 2023, the monetary ceiling on exemption of leave encashment received on retirement by a non-government employee under Section 10(10AA) is:
o: ₹25 lakh
₹3 lakh
₹20 lakh
₹10 lakh
e: The limit of ₹3 lakh, fixed in 2002, was raised to ₹25 lakh by CBDT notification effective 1 April 2023. Government employees continue to enjoy full exemption.

topic: Group Insurance - Administration, Claims and Renewals
t: A group term policy earned premium of ₹10 lakh and incurred claims of ₹7.5 lakh during the year. The claims ratio is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Claims ratio = incurred claims ÷ earned premium = 7.5 ÷ 10 = 75%. This is the key figure used in experience rating at renewal.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: Rules governing the approval and operation of an approved superannuation fund are contained in which part of the Fourth Schedule to the Income-tax Act?
o: Part A
Part C
Part B
Part D
e: Part A of the Fourth Schedule deals with recognised provident funds, Part B with approved superannuation funds and Part C with approved gratuity funds.

topic: Tax Aspects of Group & Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: The additional deduction available for an individual's own contribution to NPS Tier I under Section 80CCD(1B), over and above the Section 80C limit, is up to:
e: Section 80CCD(1B) provides an extra deduction of up to ₹50,000 for self-contribution to NPS Tier I, in addition to the ₹1.5 lakh overall ceiling under Section 80CCE.

t: Under Ind AS 19, remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability (actuarial gains and losses and return on plan assets excluding net interest) are:
o: Charged to profit or loss in the year they arise
Deferred and amortised over the average remaining working life
Shown as an extraordinary item
Recognised in other comprehensive income and never reclassified to profit or loss
e: Ind AS 19 requires remeasurements to go to OCI without subsequent recycling. Under AS 15 (Revised), by contrast, actuarial gains and losses are recognised immediately in the statement of profit and loss.

t: The actuarial method prescribed by both AS 15 (Revised) and Ind AS 19 for measuring defined benefit obligations is:
o: Projected Unit Credit method
Entry Age Normal method
Attained Age method
Aggregate funding method
e: Both standards mandate the Projected Unit Credit method, under which each period of service gives rise to an additional unit of benefit, measured with projected salaries.

t: Which of the following is treated as a 'short-term employee benefit' under AS 15 (Revised) and Ind AS 19?
o: Gratuity payable on retirement
Long-service award payable after 15 years
Annual leave and bonus expected to be settled wholly within 12 months after the end of the period
Post-retirement medical benefits
e: Short-term benefits are those expected to be settled wholly before twelve months after the end of the period in which service is rendered, such as wages, bonus and compensated absences falling within that window.

topic: Investment Pattern for Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: Under the Ministry of Finance investment pattern (2015) applicable to non-government provident, superannuation and gratuity funds, the maximum permitted allocation to equity and related instruments is:
e: The 2015 pattern allows 5% to 15% in equities and related instruments, 45% to 50% in government securities, 35% to 45% in debt instruments, up to 5% in short-term debt and up to 5% in asset-backed instruments.

topic: Investment Pattern for Retirement Benefit Schemes
t: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation makes its equity investments mainly through:
o: Exchange-traded funds tracking indices such as Nifty 50 and Sensex
Direct purchase of individual shares selected by the CBT
Equity-linked savings schemes of mutual funds
Unlisted private equity funds
e: EPFO began equity investment in 2015 and routes it through index-based ETFs managed by fund houses, rather than picking individual stocks.

t: Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the minimum continuous service required for eligibility is five years. In which situation is this requirement waived?
o: Resignation after four years and eight months
Retrenchment after three years of service
Termination of employment due to death or disablement
Voluntary retirement after four years
e: Section 4(1) proviso dispenses with the five-year condition where employment ends because of death or disablement due to accident or disease; in such cases gratuity is payable for the service rendered.

t: A gratuity of ₹1 lakh is expected to be paid in exactly one year. Ignoring decrements, its present value at a discount rate of 7% is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). PV = ₹1,00,000 ÷ 1.07 = ₹93,458 (rounded). ₹92,593 would be the value at 8% and ₹93,000 is a flat 7% deduction, which is incorrect.

t: The maximum gratuity payable under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, as currently notified, is:
o: ₹10 lakh
₹20 lakh
₹25 lakh
₹30 lakh
e: The ceiling was raised from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh with effect from 29 March 2018 through the Payment of Gratuity (Amendment) Act, 2018 and notification.

t: An employee covered by the Payment of Gratuity Act retires after 20 years and 7 months of service with last drawn wages (basic plus DA) of ₹40,000 per month. Gratuity payable is:
e: Service of 20 years 7 months is rounded to 21 years since the fraction exceeds six months. Gratuity = ₹40,000 × 15/26 × 21 = ₹4,84,615.

t: The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 applies to every establishment specified in Schedule I or notified by the Government that employs:
o: 10 or more persons
50 or more persons
100 or more persons
20 or more persons
e: The Act applies to factories and notified establishments employing 20 or more persons; once covered, an establishment remains covered even if its strength later falls below 20.

t: An employee draws basic wages of ₹25,000 per month. The employer's contribution diverted to the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 (without any option for higher pension) is:
e: EPS contribution is 8.33% of wages subject to the statutory ceiling of ₹15,000, i.e. ₹1,250 per month. The balance of the employer's 12% (₹3,000 − ₹1,250 = ₹1,750) goes to the provident fund.

t: The monthly member's pension under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 is computed as:
o: Pensionable salary × pensionable service ÷ 60
Last drawn salary × 50%
Pensionable salary × pensionable service ÷ 70
Average salary of last 5 years × 1/3
e: Paragraph 12 of EPS 1995 gives the formula pensionable salary × pensionable service ÷ 70, where pensionable salary is the average of the last 60 months (subject to ceiling) and service is in years.

t: On normal exit from NPS at age 60, a subscriber with a corpus above the small-corpus threshold must:
o: Use at least 40% of the corpus to buy an annuity; up to 60% may be withdrawn as a tax-free lump sum
Use at least 80% of the corpus to buy an annuity
Withdraw the entire corpus as lump sum
Keep the corpus invested until age 70 compulsorily
e: PFRDA exit rules require a minimum 40% annuitisation on superannuation; the remaining 60% lump sum is exempt under Section 10(12A). The 80% annuity rule applies to premature exit before 60.

t: The IRDAI portal through which a policyholder can escalate an unresolved grievance against an insurer is:
o: Bima Sugam
Bima Bharosa
Bima Vahak
Bima Vistaar
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) is the grievance portal; Bima Sugam is the marketplace, Bima Vahak the women-led distribution channel and Bima Vistaar the combined rural product.

t: Which of the following is NOT an actuarial assumption normally used in valuing a gratuity liability?
o: Discount rate
Future salary escalation rate
Employee attrition (withdrawal) rate
The employer's profit for the current financial year
e: Gratuity valuation depends on financial assumptions (discount rate, salary growth) and demographic assumptions (mortality, withdrawal, retirement age). The employer's profit has no bearing on the liability.

t: In India, the discount rate used to value a defined benefit obligation under AS 15 (Revised) or Ind AS 19 should be based on:
o: The rate of return earned on the gratuity fund last year
Market yields on government bonds with a term consistent with the liability
The bank rate announced by RBI
The rate of interest declared by EPFO
e: Both standards require the discount rate to reflect market yields at the balance sheet date on government bonds (used in India in the absence of a deep corporate bond market) of a currency and term consistent with the obligation.

t: A gratuity scheme had a defined benefit obligation of ₹100 lakh at the start of the year. Current service cost is ₹10 lakh, the discount rate is 7%, benefits paid during the year are ₹5 lakh and an actuarial loss of ₹3 lakh arose. The closing obligation is:
o: ₹112 lakh
₹110 lakh
₹115 lakh
₹122 lakh
e: Closing DBO = 100 + 10 (service cost) + 7 (interest at 7% on 100) − 5 (benefits paid) + 3 (actuarial loss) = ₹115 lakh.

t: The mortality table most commonly adopted by Indian actuaries for valuing employee benefit liabilities such as gratuity is:
o: Indian Assured Lives Mortality (IALM) 2012-14
LIC (1994-96) Annuitants table
Indian Individual Annuitants Mortality 2012-15
UK A1967-70 table
e: IALM 2012-14, published by the Institute of Actuaries of India, is the standard base for active-life mortality in employee benefit valuations; annuitant tables are used for pension-in-payment valuations.

topic: Group Insurance - Administration, Claims and Renewals
t: Which set of documents is normally required to settle a death claim under an employer-employee group term policy?
o: Original master policy, employee's appointment letter and bank passbook
Claim form, death certificate and employer's certification of membership and sum assured on the date of death
Post-mortem report, police FIR and income-tax return of the deceased
Nominee's birth certificate and the member's salary slips for 5 years
e: Group death claims are simple: a claim intimation, proof of death and the master policyholder's confirmation of membership and cover are the core requirements. Police reports are needed only for unnatural deaths.

topic: Group Insurance - Administration, Claims and Renewals
t: A group term policy for an employer-employee group earned premium of ₹10 lakh. Claims paid were ₹6 lakh and the insurer's expense loading is 20% of premium. If the profit-sharing formula refunds 50% of the surplus, the experience refund is:
e: Surplus = ₹10 lakh − ₹6 lakh claims − ₹2 lakh expenses = ₹2 lakh. Refund at 50% = ₹1,00,000.

topic: Group Insurance - Administration, Claims and Renewals
t: At the annual renewal of a one-year group term policy, the insurer is entitled to:
o: Revise the premium rate based on the group's claims experience and changed membership profile
Refuse to cover any member who has made a claim
Convert the policy into an individual endowment policy
Demand individual medical reports from all members
e: Renewal re-rating on experience and demographic change is the essence of yearly renewable group term business; cover cannot be denied selectively to members who have claimed (e.g. for critical illness riders).

t: Catastrophe reinsurance is particularly relevant for group insurance because:
o: Group policies are always written on a with-profit basis
Many members of one group may die in a single event, such as a factory accident, creating an accumulation of claims
Group policies have no free cover limit
IRDAI mandates it for every group policy
e: Group lives are concentrated at one location or in one occupation, so one event can cause multiple claims. Catastrophe (cat) cover protects the insurer against this accumulation risk.

t: An insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within how many days of receipt?
o: 7 days
14 days
30 days
45 days
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 14 days under the 2024 regulations; thereafter the policyholder may approach Bima Bharosa or the Ombudsman.

t: Under a surplus reinsurance treaty for group term business, the insurer:
o: Cedes a fixed percentage of every life insured
Cedes only lives that fail medical underwriting
Cedes the full sum assured of every member above the free cover limit
Retains sums assured up to its retention limit per life and cedes the excess to the reinsurer
e: A surplus treaty transfers only the portion of each life's sum assured that exceeds the ceding company's retention; a quota share treaty, by contrast, cedes a fixed proportion of every risk.

t: To obtain approval of a gratuity fund under Part C of the Fourth Schedule to the Income-tax Act, the fund must be:
o: Established under an irrevocable trust for the exclusive benefit of employees
Registered with IRDAI as a pension fund
Managed only by the employer's finance department
Invested entirely in the employer's own shares
e: An approved gratuity fund must be an irrevocable trust in connection with a trade or undertaking carried on in India, with the employer not able to recover the contributions, and investments made per prescribed norms.

t: Which of the following is NOT permitted to the trustees of an approved gratuity fund?
o: Taking a group gratuity policy from a life insurer in the name of the trust
Appointing an actuary to value the liability annually
Lending the fund's monies to the employer company
Investing in the pattern prescribed under Rule 67
e: Loans to the employer are prohibited since the fund must remain beyond the employer's reach. Insuring with a life insurer, actuarial valuation and investment under Rule 67 are all normal trustee functions.

t: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) provides a life cover of ₹2 lakh for persons aged 18 to 50 at an annual premium (since 1 June 2022) of:
e: PMJJBY premium was revised from ₹330 to ₹436 per annum from June 2022; cover is ₹2 lakh on death from any cause, renewable each year from 1 June to 31 May.

t: The annual premium for Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), which provides ₹2 lakh accidental death and total disability cover, is:
e: PMSBY premium was raised from ₹12 to ₹20 per annum from June 2022. It covers persons aged 18 to 70 for ₹2 lakh on accidental death or total disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.

t: Under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948, the current rates of contribution (since 1 July 2019) are:
o: Employee 0.75% and employer 3.25% of wages
Employee 1.75% and employer 4.75% of wages
Employee 12% and employer 12% of wages
Employee 1% and employer 4% of wages
e: The rates were reduced from 1.75%/4.75% to 0.75%/3.25% in July 2019. Employees earning up to ₹176 per day are exempt from their share, and the wage ceiling for coverage is ₹21,000 per month.
